newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: PM SAYS HINDMARSH ISLAND ISSUE BECOME A "JOKE"
The Prime Minister, John Howard, has told his colleagues the Hindmarsh Island bridge issue is becoming an absolute joke.
The Senate last night rejected the Government's Hindmarsh Island bill that was aimed at allowing the bridge project to proceed.
Mr Howard says that means there's now likely to be a fifth inquiry into the bridge proposal.
He's told the party room he can't believe that it's happening again.
QUEENSLAND CYCLONE COULD BRING MORE FLOODING
The weather bureau says it looks as though tropical cyclone Gillian will only result in useful rains along the central Queensland coast.
The bureau's senior forecaster, Greg Bond, says current indications are that the category one cyclone is not likely to intensify strongly in the next 24 hours.
He says if the category one cyclone continues on its current course it isn't likely to cross the coast until tomorrow night or Thursday morning, prompting possible flood rains south of Townsville.
Gillian is currently about 370 kilometres east north-east of Cairns and moving slowly in a south south-westerly direction. - - - -
PROPERTY THREATENED BY FLOODWATERS
In Western Australia, another pastoral property in the West Pilbara is in danger of inundation from floodwaters.
The State Emergency Service is monitoring water from the swollen Ashburton River, as it approaches Eurala station, about 35 kilometres south west of Onslow.
Water is now within 200 metres the homestead, but the SES says it's still too early to predict whether the house will be flooded.
Meanwhile, repairs are continuing on a severely flood-damaged section of North West Coastal Highway, near the Ashburton Bridge.
Two 70-metre sections of the road were destroyed in the floods, and the highway is expected to re-open early tomorrow morning.
NO REFUEL FOR WARSHIP AS CYCLONE THREATENS
The Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority says cyclone Gillian has forced plans to refuel a United States Ammunition ship in Cleveland Bay to be shelved.
Authority representative, Craig Sambell, says the U.S.N.S. KILUAUEA will weigh anchor and head south to Gladstone.
Mr Sambell says it would be foolish to proceed with such a sensitive operation with the initial cyclone warning in place.
The plans to refuel the ship within the boundaries of the marine park has drawn criticism from the Democrats.
VALUABLE STAMP COULD HAVE BEEN LEFT IN PHOTOCOPIER
The District Court in Perth has been told a valuable stamp that disappeared from the office of former Premier Brian Burke may have been left in a photocopy machine.
The revelation came during the former Premier's trial on charges of stealing up to 122-thousand dollars from the Labor Party while he was leader in the 1980s.
The prosecution alleges Mr Burke used the money to buy stamps for his personal collection.
He has pleaded not guilty.
One of his former staff members Bruno Santorelli told the Court the missing stamp was worth between five and ten-thousand dollars.
Today he told the Court Mr Burke had said there was not much point in calling in the police after an internal search had failed to find it.
However Mr Santorelli admitted that he told Mr Burke it was a possibility the stamp had been left in a photocoping machine.
The trial is continuing.
NSW PREMIER SAYS PM'S MISSED HIS MARK
The Premier says John Howard has missed an opportunity to make his mark in history by not supporting an Australian republic.
Mr Carr says the Prime Minister lacks a sense of history by downplaying his own proposal for a constitutional convention.
At the launch of a new national newspaper, The Republican, Mr Carr said he would have welcomed a surprise display of visionary leadership.
NSW POLICE MINISTER SUPPORTS SACKED POLICE
Police Minister Paul Whelan says he now supports sacked police officers being able to appeal against their dismissal to the state industrial commission.
The Police Assocation and Police Royal Commissioner James Wood, who recommended the abolition of appeals, have been meeting to discuss the dispute over the past two days.
Mr Whelan says he wants to set up a working party to thrash out the isue over the next two weeks.
He says the appeal process will have to be streamlined.
